records.text: A 48-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis presents with dyspepsia and bloating. Endoscopy reveals erythematous mucosa. Histopathology shows serrated gastric pits, foveolar hyperplasia, low mucin in surface epithelial cells, and ectatic superficial capillaries.

A 56-year-old African American woman presents with hair loss on the vertex of her scalp, a history of tight hairstyles, and an itching sensation. A punch biopsy reveals the features shown in the photomicrograph. The most likely diagnosis is central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia.

The abnormal cell with eosinophilic and basophilic granules, located near the center of the photomicrograph of a bone marrow aspirate, is strongly associated with a recurrent cytogenetic abnormality. This finding is typically observed in acute myeloid leukemia with inv 16 or t(16;16).

This is a histopathology image of a lollipop lesion associated with Castleman disease, specifically the hyaline vascular type. It features a broad mantle zone with concentric layers of peripheral lymphocytes and thick hyalinized vessels penetrating the germinal center.

A histopathology image of scrotal Paget’s disease, characterized as an adenocarcinoma in situ. The primary form is more common than secondary from underlying malignancy. Treatment typically involves wide surgical excision, with chemotherapy or radiotherapy as options.

A histopathology image of a hemangioma shows an increased number of vessels, both normal and abnormal. The vascular structures contain red blood cells or transudate and are lined by a monolayer of non-atypical endothelial cells.

This histopathology image illustrates Toxoplasma, often due to reactivation of latent infection in organ transplant recipients. Donor-transmitted or de novo infections can occur. Common presentations include retinochoroiditis, cerebritis, pneumonitis, and disseminated disease.

This histopathology image of nodular fasciitis features bland spindle cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm arranged in a vague storiform pattern, interspersed with lymphocytes and extravasated red blood cells. Smooth muscle actin highlights the myofibroblasts.

A common finding in gynecologic cytology: fungal organisms on a pap test. Morphologically consistent with Candida species, showing yeast forms and elongated pseudohyphae. Symptoms may include itching and discharge.

A benign change called deciduosis in a cervix biopsy, often seen in pregnancy due to high progesterone levels. Common in patients with cervical dysplasia history. The image displays cervix tissue with decidualized stroma resembling endometrium.

A histopathology image of a foreign body granuloma with polarizable material, histiocytes, and giant cells. Common causes include suture, wood splinters, tattoo ink, and insect fragments. Hair and keratin can also trigger this reaction.

Histopathology image of clear cell carcinoma in the ovary. Neoplastic pieces display papillary structures and solid tumor cell growth with distinct features. Immunohistochemistry reveals PAX8 and Napsin expression. Associated with endometriosis and Lynch syndrome.

Metastatic breast cancer to the brain in a patient with invasive ductal carcinoma. Histopathology images show cohesive malignant cells in white matter. Expression of GATA3 and HER2 indicates breast primary tumor. Brain metastasis commonly from lung, breast, colon, and melanoma. Personal history aids diagnosis.

Atypical mitosis in a case of breast carcinoma shows spindle multipolarity. This occurs during metaphase when a cell develops more than two spindle poles, leading to abnormal chromosome distribution. Immunohistochemical stains are essential tools for pathologists. Correct interpretation involves assessing cell type, location, staining intensity, and the number of stained cells. Always verify the control tissue, as its intensity may vary between laboratories. Request a panel of markers to confirm or rule out differential diagnoses, as some tumors may not stain as expected if poorly differentiated.

Gynecomastia has a bimodal distribution, primarily affecting newborns and the elderly. It is linked to conditions that elevate serum estrogen levels, such as liver cirrhosis and hyperthyroidism. Infants may develop this condition due to estrogen exposure in utero.

This image shows cystitis glandularis, a benign change located just beneath the urothelium, not adenocarcinoma. Key features include its superficial location, absence of cytologic atypia, and minimal mucin production.

This histopathology image shows micropapillary morphology, which accounts for 1-2% of urothelial carcinoma. It features small nests without vascular cores and inverted polarity within lacunar spaces. Subgemmal neurogenous plaque (SNP) is a neural plexus near taste buds in the tongue's papillae. Hyperplasia can mimic other lesions, causing symptoms like burning or pain. Biopsy is advised to differentiate from potential malignancies.

Melanoacanthoma is a benign, pigmented oral lesion with melanocytes in the epithelium. It presents in Black females in their 30s-40s, with dark pigmentation that can mimic melanoma. Typically unilateral, it may resolve without surgery, often biopsied to rule out melanoma.

Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is a malignant salivary gland neoplasm with distinct cell types forming cystic and solid growth patterns. Most cases involve major salivary glands, with specific genetic translocations. Different grades exhibit varying histological features and clinical outcomes. Immunohistochemistry can aid in diagnosis.

A histopathology image of a tiger kidney. Kidneys filter blood, regulate water, hormones, electrolytes, and pressure. Kidney disease is common in cats, with certain breeds at higher risk. A cross-section of small intestine villi shows goblet cells secreting acid mucous to protect epithelial cells. Acid mucous is present in GI and respiratory tracts, except the stomach, which has neutral mucous to counteract stomach acid. Image from a dog.

A histopathology image of glomeruli in a lion's kidney stained with Periodic Acid Schiff. The filtration process in the kidney begins in the glomerulus, where waste products are filtered out and travel down to the tubules. Important substances are returned to the bloodstream, while wastes are excreted in urine.

Asteroid bodies are not specific for sarcoidosis. Lung shows granulomas, giant cell infiltrate with asteroid bodies in almost every giant cell. Fungal hyphae identified without GMS stain.
In cirrhotic liver, reticulin helps detect early HCC. Reticulin is fragmented in HCC but defines hepatocytic plates in non-tumoral nodules.

Histopathology image of a keloid showing abnormal scar tissue proliferation beyond injury boundaries. Common sites include anterior chest, shoulders, upper back, back of neck, and cheeks. A histopathology image of multiple myeloma, a rare plasma cell malignancy with bone involvement. The tumor cells are monoclonal, producing abnormal proteins. EBV+ PTLD DLBCL: extranodal sites, often GI tract involvement, histology resembles lymphomas in immunocompetent patients, EBER+ (shown). Decreasing immunosuppression may resolve, but relapse is common.
